judgment.rationale: The attached sample begins with FF FE and nearly half its bytes are NULs. Current source re-encodes decoded text with the source encoding before passing it to a JavaScript UTF-8 decoder, directly explaining the rendered NUL boxes.
evidence: The attached Minimal.reg is 78 bytes, begins FF FE, and has a 0.487 NUL-byte ratio.
The issue reproduces on 0.101.2362.0 and the Windows built-in text preview decodes the same file correctly.
MonacoPreviewHandlerControl.cs base64-encodes encodingToUse.GetBytes(fileContent), while Monaco/index.html decodes the payload with decodeURIComponent/UTF-8 byte semantics.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused fix that normalizes the decoded string to UTF-8 for the Monaco transport and adds UTF-16 regression coverage.

fix_assessment.rationale: No merged or active fix was found; attachment bytes and current source establish a narrow encoding-boundary defect.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize Monaco transport bytes to UTF-8 after source decoding
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The handler decodes the source file into a .NET string but then base64-encodes that string using the original file encoding. Monaco/index.html interprets the base64 bytes as UTF-8, so UTF-16LE NUL bytes become visible characters.
plan: Keep BOM/charset detection for reading the source file.
Encode the resulting Unicode string with Encoding.UTF8 before base64 transport to Monaco.
Add tests using BOM-marked UTF-16LE .reg content and non-ASCII text to prove the transport round-trips without NULs or mojibake.
verification: Decode the attached Minimal.reg and assert the Monaco payload produces “Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00” with no U+0000 characters.
Retain UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM, and legacy code-page preview tests.
Build and run Monaco preview handler unit/UI coverage.

confidence.rationale: The attachment bytes and the source/JavaScript encoding mismatch directly explain the exact symptom.

issue_context.summary: The Monaco preview handler correctly reads a BOM-marked UTF-16LE .reg file into text, then re-encodes that text as UTF-16 bytes while the embedded JavaScript always decodes the base64 payload as UTF-8, exposing every UTF-16 NUL byte.
known_information: The attached .reg file is BOM-marked UTF-16LE and reproduces on 0.101.2362.0.
UTF-8 input and the Windows built-in preview handler display correctly.
The current handler decodes through CharsetDetector/StreamReader, then base64-encodes using the detected source encoding.
inferences: The source decoding succeeds; corruption is introduced by using source-encoding bytes in a transport whose JavaScript decoder assumes UTF-8.
issue_context.analysis: The byte-level attachment check and both ends of the transport agree: UTF-16 NUL bytes are intentionally preserved in base64 and then misinterpreted by the JavaScript decoder.
